name: Energy Vault Holdings, Inc.

profile.description: Energy Vault Holdings develops and deploys utility-scale energy storage, including B-Vault battery systems for short-duration storage, G-Vault gravity storage for long-duration needs, and H-Vault hydrogen/hybrid solutions, supported by Vault-OS energy management and the AI-based Vault-Bidder dispatch optimization software. The company is pivoting from build-and-transfer projects toward an own-and-operate independent power producer model, with about 60% of its ~$2B backlog tied to owned infrastructure. Co-founder Robert Piconi serves as Chairman and CEO.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Energy Vault pivoted from its signature gravity-tower concept toward battery storage and an own-and-operate IPP model, lifting revenue from $46.2M in FY2024 to $203.7M in FY2025 and posting Q2 2026 revenue of $17.4M (+104% YoY) on Australian BESS projects [1][3]. Gravity storage itself remains contested - critics note reduced round-trip efficiency, tower height, and duration claims versus original marketing [5]. AI Deployment (1/2): The Vault-Bidder product uses AI on live asset and market data for dispatch and revenue optimization, but no quantified AI revenue or savings were disclosed [4]. Market Share (1/2): A meaningful but sub-scale player in a crowded BESS integration market dominated by larger integrators. Pipeline (2/2): Backlog of about $2B (+107% YoY) is expected to approach $3B by year-end 2026, with FY2026 revenue guidance raised to $270-310M and 2027 expectations due on the November call [1][2]. R&D Intensity (0/1): R&D was cut from $42.6M (FY2022) to $14.6M (FY2025), signaling de-prioritization of proprietary technology development [3].

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Energy Vault states that its employees share a passion to combat climate change through innovation in energy storage - clear and purpose-linked, but similar to many clean-energy peers [6]. Community Impact (0/2): No distinctive community investment program with quantified impact was found. Employee Retention (0/2): No retention or tenure data was found, and FMP lists just 142 full-time employees, small for a company targeting $270-310M of revenue [4]. Insider Buying (1/2): CEO Piconi made an open-market purchase of 12,500 shares at $3.21 on March 31, 2026 ($40,120) - a positive but modest signal [6].

infrastructure.label: WEAK
infrastructure.analysis: Mechanically scored on 5 of 7 growth metrics; 5yr revenue CAGR is excluded because revenue was zero in FY2020-FY2021, and Forward PEG is unavailable [3]. Revenue growth of 104% YoY (Q2 2026) scores 1.0, but D/E of 751% (floor 300%), ROE of -178.6% (2x weight), profit margin of -48.6%, and a negative forward P/E of -22.7 all score 0 [1][7]. Weighted 1.0/6 = 1.7, rounded to 2. The leverage reflects project-level debt for owned assets; FY2025 net loss was $103.6M [3]. Liquidity floor cleared: 4.42M avg volume x $3.09 = $13.7M daily [7].

ai_resilience.label: LOW RISK
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (8/9): Energy Vault builds and owns physical grid-scale storage assets - battery systems, gravity structures, and hybrid plants - that AI cannot substitute, and surging electricity demand from AI data centers increases the need for grid firming and storage capacity [1][2]. No analyst commentary identifies AI as a displacement risk. AI Opportunity (0/1): Vault-Bidder applies AI to dispatch optimization, but no quantified AI-related revenue was disclosed, so the tiebreaker point is not awarded [4].

infinite_game.summary: Energy Vault's founding cause - decarbonizing the grid through storage innovation - has survived the partial failure of its original gravity-tower vision, which Sinek would see as a sign the cause is bigger than any one product. The company's willingness to pivot to batteries and then to owning assets shows real existential flexibility. Weighing against it are a history of contested claims, a sharp reduction in R&D, and little evidence of a high-trust culture.

just_cause.analysis: Just Cause (2/3): Combating climate change through energy storage is a genuine, service-oriented cause, and the company's pivots from gravity to batteries to owned infrastructure trace back to that purpose rather than to a single product [1][6]. It has not been validated over decades, and early overstatement of gravity storage capabilities undercut credibility [5].

trusting_teams.analysis: Trusting Teams (1/2): Co-founder Piconi has led continuously since founding and has emphasized that execution 'really starts with people,' citing perseverance and humility [6]. No employee-sentiment or retention data was found to indicate exceptional trust, so this is scored as adequate.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Worthy Rivals (0/1): The company's public posture toward critics has been combative - its 2022 response to Bleecker Street Research labeled the report 'inaccurate and misleading' - and no commentary was found acknowledging competitors as benchmarks for improvement [5].

existential_flexibility.analysis: Existential Flexibility (2/2): Energy Vault has reinvented itself twice - from a gravity-storage technology company to a technology-agnostic battery integrator, and now to an own-and-operate IPP with 60% of backlog in owned infrastructure for long-term recurring revenue [1][6]. These are fundamental business-model shifts, not incremental extensions.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Courage to Lead (1/2): Shifting toward owned assets sacrifices near-term build-and-transfer revenue for long-term recurring cash flow, and the CEO bought shares in the open market in March 2026 despite a 'Strong Sell' analyst consensus [1][6]. Cutting R&D by roughly two-thirds since FY2022 is the opposite of investing through a downturn [3].

investment_thesis: Energy Vault is scaling rapidly into grid storage demand. FY2025 revenue rose to $203.7M from $46.2M, Q2 2026 revenue grew 104% to $17.4M, and FY2026 guidance was raised to $270-310M with gross margin narrowed to 20-25% [1][3]. Backlog roughly doubled to about $2B and is expected to approach $3B by year-end, with 60% in owned-and-operated projects that generate long-term recurring revenue and 40% in build-and-transfer contracts expected to convert within 12-18 months [1][2]. Electricity demand from AI data centers and renewables integration supports structural growth in storage, and CEO Piconi's March 2026 open-market purchase signals insider conviction [6].
thesis_continued: The bear case is balance sheet and execution. D/E is 751%, ROE is -178.6%, profit margin is -48.6%, and the company lost $103.6M in FY2025, so the own-and-operate model depends on continued access to project financing [3][7]. Revenue is highly lumpy - a substantial majority of second-half 2026 revenue is expected in Q4 - and guidance for year-end cash varies across sources ($140-200M vs. $160-200M) [2]. The company has a history of contested claims, including a 2022 short-seller report, investor litigation over the DG Fuels partnership, and skepticism about gravity storage economics, and analyst consensus remains 'Strong Sell' [5][6].
key_catalysts: Delivery of the raised FY2026 revenue guidance of $270-310M, with a heavily Q4-weighted second half [1][2]
Backlog growth from ~$2B toward ~$3B by year-end 2026 and 2027 outlook on the November earnings call [2]
Conversion of the 40% build-and-transfer backlog to revenue over 12-18 months and commissioning of owned assets generating recurring cash flow [1]
key_risks: Extreme leverage (D/E 751%) and persistent losses (FY2025 net loss $103.6M) make the IPP pivot dependent on project financing markets [3][7]
Lumpy, back-end-loaded revenue recognition creates high risk of quarterly misses and guidance resets [2]
Credibility overhang from the 2022 short-seller report, DG Fuels litigation, and contested gravity-storage technology claims [5]

backlog.note: Record backlog of ~$2B (+107% YoY) as of Q2 2026, guided to approach ~$3B by year-end; 60% is owned-and-operated infrastructure (long-dated recurring revenue) and 40% build-and-transfer converting in 12-18 months. Funded split and TTM book-to-bill not disclosed. Backlog-to-revenue of ~27.6 quarters (vs. FY2026 guidance midpoint of $290M) is inflated by long-dated owned-asset revenue and also signals execution risk.
